question.problem:
Find the values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for 
 $f(x)=2\sqrt{x}$ on the interval $[0,4].$
question.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous on $[0,4]$ and differentiable on $(0,4),$ hence we can apply the mean value theorem. 

So, the mean value theorem states that there exists a $c\in (0,4)$ such that

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}.
$$

Plugging in $a=0$ and $b=4$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(c) & =\frac{f(4)-f(0)}{4-0} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{4}-2\sqrt{0}}{4} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\sqrt{x})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{c}}.
$$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{c}} & =1 \\ \sqrt{c} & =1 \\ c & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
